subject: Fix CodeRabbit m_mode data race — Phase 6 atomic enforcement
summary: CodeRabbit reviewed PR #20 and flagged that reordering m_mode write before the release store on m_active is insufficient — m_mode remains a non-atomic plain mutable EnforcementMode, so concurrent reads in getStatus() can still observe torn/stale values. PR #21 applied the reordering per the PR author's interpretation but did not make m_mode atomic. The CodeRabbit suggestion explicitly stated 'Reordering the existing assignments alone is insufficient.' Fix applied: both m_active and m_mode are now std::atomic<...>. safeHonor() does m_mode.store(relaxed) then m_active.store(release); getStatus() does m_active.load(acquire) then m_mode.load(relaxed). The release/acquire pair on m_active establishes happens-before for the m_mode read, satisfying the C++11 memory model and eliminating the data race.
